issue_title: Week 1: the private preview must show what changed, not just link to it
problem_statement:
Week 1: the private preview must show what changed, not just link to it

**Parent:** #442 · **Spec:** `specs/provisioning-invisible-deployment.md` §4.2–§4.3 · **Scope:** DECISIONS #62 Week 1

## The ask (DECISIONS #62, item 5)

Every change the owner makes by talking shows a private preview that gives a **clear visual sense of the change** — a diff or a before/after — not merely a link to a built site.

## Why a link alone is not enough

A link asks a non-technical owner to spot the difference themselves. On a phone, on a page they only half remember, after a change they described in one sentence. That is the moment where "approve" stops meaning anything, and an approval that means nothing is what makes the ownership promise hollow later.

## Verified current state

`apps/mcp/lib/preview-url.ts` (97 lines) does one job and does it well: it validates a **caller-supplied** preview URL and refuses placeholder/example hosts so an agent cannot pass a fake preview off as real. It has no notion of *what changed* — there is no diff surface anywhere on the MCP.

`rewind_site` already computes a plain-language description of changed files and sections (`wouldChange.plainLanguage`, `wouldChange.sections`). That translation layer — file paths to "your hours", "your services list" — is the right precedent and should be reused, not reinvented.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For a proposed change, the owner receives a plain-language summary of what will differ — in the vocabulary of their business ("your hours", "the plumbing service description"), never file paths, hunks, or line numbers.
2. Where a visual before/after is feasible, it is offered alongside the summary; where it is not, the summary stands alone and the response says so honestly rather than implying a visual exists.
3. Nothing is invented. If the diff cannot be computed, or the preview has not built yet, say that plainly — do not describe a change that has not been verified, and do not emit a preview URL that was not returned by the platform. The existing posture in `preview-url.ts` extends here.
4. Reuses the `rewind.ts` section-naming translation rather than a second, divergent mapping. If that mapping needs to move to a shared module, move it — do not fork it.
5. Works on the MCP surface, in any client, per spec §3.5. Phone-first: the summary must be readable in a chat bubble without horizontal scrolling.
6. Contract tests with injected clients; includes the "diff unavailable" and "preview still building" paths, not just the happy case.

## Honest boundary

"Visual sense of the change" is satisfied by a *reliable, plain-language* account of the difference plus a preview link. A rendered image diff is a stretch goal, not the acceptance bar — and shipping a flaky image diff would trade the thing that must be perfect (the owner understands what they are approving) for the thing that is merely nice.
